description:
These yellow subway mosaic tiles for kitchen walls are small glazed ceramic rectangles laid in the familiar subway, or brick, pattern for backsplashes and cooking walls.

## How they look
Subway is one of the most lasting backsplash layouts, and the yellow glaze gives it a warm, sunny lift. Because the pieces are small, the wall gets more texture than standard subway tiles while keeping the same clean lines.

## Where they work
- **Behind the stove and counter**, where a glazed surface is generally easy to wipe clean of oil and masala splashes.
- **Open shelving walls**, as a bright band between upper and lower cabinets.
- **Small kitchens**, where a warm colour can make a narrow space feel friendlier without needing a busy pattern.

Pair it with white or wooden cabinets and a white or light grey grout for a fresh look, or a darker grout if you want joints that hide stains.

## Good to know
Behind a gas stove, keep the recommended gap between the burner and the wall, and use a grout that can be scrubbed. Plan the layout so cut pieces sit at the ends, out of sight.

## See it before you order
Pak Clay shows its range at the Lahore head office on Walton Road (opposite Packages Mall Gate 2) and at G-04 Civic Center, Gulberg Greens, Islamabad, Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 9 pm. Ask for a [free sample on WhatsApp](https://wa.me/923004617715) and hold it next to your counter top, then get a dated quote for your wall area. Browse more in the [kitchen wall mosaic range](/categories/mosaic-kitchen-wall-tiles).

faqs.q: Are glazed mosaic tiles good behind a stove?
faqs.a: Glazed ceramic is a common backsplash surface because it is generally easy to wipe clean of oil. Use a scrubbable grout and keep the standard safety gap between the burner and the wall.

faqs.q: Subway mosaic or full-size subway tiles?
faqs.a: Subway mosaic gives the same brick layout in smaller pieces, so it has more texture and works well around sockets and windows. Full-size subway tiles have fewer grout lines and are quicker to clean.
